edge: Place break inside a nested procedural block that remains within a loop.
negative: Use break outside every loop.
positive: Place break in the body of a loop.

edge: Break from a multidimensional foreach and verify all dimension iteration terminates.
positive: Break from a loop body and verify no later iteration or loop step occurs.

edge: Introduce one unsigned item among signed expressions and verify unsigned treatment applies to all.
positive: Compare all-signed expressions whose extension and match reflect signed treatment.

edge: Make the longest expression an item other than the first.
positive: Use controlling and item expressions of different widths whose match depends on common longest-width conversion.

edge: Use a sized signed constant case expression against mixed-width item expressions.
positive: Use case (1) with variable bit-select item expressions to implement a priority selection.

edge: Use a single default without its optional colon.
negative: Place two default items in one case statement.
positive: Use case statements with zero and one default item.

edge: Mix ? with ordinary digits and explicit Z digits in one case item.
positive: Use ? digits in binary literals of casez and casex items.

edge: Place a default between source items and verify it is not part of comparison search.
notes: Avoid scheduling races when exposing side effects.
positive: Use deterministic counters to verify one controlling evaluation followed by source-order item evaluations.

edge: Contrast X with Z at one bit and verify the item does not match.
positive: Match item expressions containing X and Z bits exactly against the case expression.

edge: Make every membership comparison return 0 or X and verify default executes.
positive: Use multiple case-inside items to observe ordering required by the selected qualification.

edge: Produce a 1'bx membership result and verify that item does not match.
positive: Use ranges and wildcard values whose inside result is 1'b1 and verify selection.

edge: Exercise no match both with a default and without one.
positive: Make two source-ordered items match and verify only the first statement executes.

edge: Place a default among items and verify it is ignored during matching.
notes: Avoid scheduling races when observing evaluation.
positive: Use deterministic side effects to verify one tested-expression evaluation followed by source-order tests.

edge: Verify binding occurs before filter evaluation by referencing the bound value in the filter.
negative: Make the pattern match but the filter evaluate to zero, X, or Z.
positive: Match a pattern and use a bound identifier in a true filter to select the item.

edge: Use a pattern item without its optional filter.
negative: Reference one item's pattern identifier from a different case item.
positive: Bind an identifier, reference it in the item's &&& filter and statement, and reuse its spelling in another item.

edge: Exercise no selected item both with and without a default.
positive: Make multiple items selectable and verify only the source-first selected statement executes.

edge: Use filters to reject otherwise matching patterns so no item is selected.
notes: Do not depend on diagnostic wording.
positive: Cause no item to select under priority and unique and verify a violation.

edge: Use differently shaped nested patterns that still have the same contextual type.
negative: Use one case-item pattern of a different structure or tagged-union type.
positive: Use multiple patterns all matching the tested structure type.

edge: Make overlapping patterns differ only by filters that both evaluate true.
notes: Do not depend on diagnostic wording.
positive: Make two items select under unique and verify an overlap violation.

edge: Exercise ignored bits in both a tagged-union tag and a nested member.
negative: Verify casez-matches does not ignore an X bit.
positive: Use casez-matches with Z in tag/member comparisons and casex-matches with X and Z.

edge: Change an item expression between successive executions of the case statement.
notes: Avoid side effects when testing only nonconstant-expression legality.
positive: Use runtime variables and function calls as the case expression and item expressions.

edge: Use optional colons on default items and a null statement as an item body.
negative: Use a pattern item in ordinary case without matches, or a range-list item without inside.
positive: Parse ordinary case, casez, casex, case-matches, and case-inside forms with their corresponding item syntax.

edge: Use multiple ignored positions split between the case expression and item expression.
negative: Verify that X is not a do-not-care in casez.
positive: Match casez with Z on each side in turn, and casex with X and Z on each side in turn.

edge: Use a binding from the first match as the expression in a second match.
negative: Reference the binding in the alternative expression.
positive: Bind an identifier in a match clause and use it in a later clause and consequent expression.

edge: Produce an ambiguous predicate through a Boolean filter and verify conditional-operator ambiguous-result merging.
positive: Exercise true and false pattern predicates and verify selection of the consequent or alternative.

edge: Verify a clause with a side effect is not evaluated after an earlier clause fails.
positive: Use a successful match followed by a true Boolean clause in a conditional expression.

edge: Place continue inside a nested procedural block that remains within a loop.
negative: Use continue outside every loop.
positive: Place continue in a loop body.

edge: Continue in a multidimensional foreach and verify it advances from the current index tuple rather than an inferred inner dimension.
positive: Continue from a for body and verify the step executes before the next condition test.

edge: Nest two unmatched if statements followed by one else and observe association with the inner if.
positive: Use begin-end around an inner unmatched if so a following else associates with the outer if.

edge: Use an X or Z post-test condition and verify termination after the first body execution.
positive: Start with a false condition and verify the body executes once before termination.

edge: Use a single entry in each list and then multiple comma-separated entries.
positive: Use multiple initialized variables and mix assignment, increment, and function-call entries in the step list.

edge: Use the same externally declared variable in sequential loops without introducing parallel races.
notes: The paragraph's parallel-process race warning does not prescribe a deterministic result.
positive: Declare a control variable in an enclosing block and assign it in the for initialization.

edge: Declare several identifiers under one data type in the local-declaration form.
negative: Assign a predeclared control and locally declare another control in the same initialization list.
positive: Declare all initialization controls locally, and separately assign only predeclared controls.

edge: Chain three declarations where each initializer uses an earlier variable.
negative: Reference a later-declared loop variable from an earlier initializer.
positive: Declare i first and initialize j from i in the same for initialization.

edge: Run parallel activations of a subroutine containing a locally declared for control and verify their controls are independent.
notes: Use synchronization to avoid introducing races when observing parallel activations.
positive: Enter a loop declaration scope on separate activations and verify each activation has its own automatic control variable.

edge: Contrast a declaration initializer with an assignment-only initializer, which creates no implicit block.
negative: Reference an unlabelled loop-local control outside its implicit scope.
positive: Declare a control in a labeled for initialization and reference it through the loop's named scope where permitted.

edge: Exercise omitted initialization, condition, and step separately, and conditions evaluating X or Z.
positive: Record initialization, condition, body, and step side effects to verify their order across iterations.

edge: Iterate an empty string and verify no index values are produced.
positive: Iterate packed, unpacked, multidimensional, and string variables.

edge: Omit all trailing dimension positions and their commas.
negative: Provide more loop-variable positions than array dimensions.
positive: Iterate selected dimensions of a multidimensional array by leaving an interior index position empty.

edge: Use a hierarchical array identifier containing indexed selections but no call.
negative: Use a function call in the foreach array-designating identifier.
positive: Use a plain array identifier or hierarchical array identifier in foreach.

edge: Use synchronized parallel activations to distinguish automatic index storage.
notes: Avoid races when observing parallel activations.
positive: Invoke a foreach-containing automatic context more than once and verify each activation has independent index variables.

edge: Explicitly cast an index to a type different from its automatic cast type.
positive: Use fixed-array and associative-array foreach indices in arithmetic expressions and verify their prescribed expression types.

edge: Use identifiers differing only beyond a shared prefix.
negative: Use the array identifier itself as a foreach index variable.
positive: Use distinct array and index identifiers.

edge: Pass the index to an input argument without modifying it.
negative: Assign to, increment, or decrement a foreach index variable in the body.
positive: Read the foreach index to access and compute array elements.

edge: Use the same index spelling in separate foreach scopes.
negative: Reference an unlabelled foreach index outside its loop scope.
positive: Label a foreach and refer to an index through the named loop scope where permitted.

edge: Contrast index types from fixed-range and specifically typed associative dimensions.
positive: Iterate a specifically typed associative array and use the index in a context that reveals the matching index type.

edge: Skip an interior dimension and verify nesting/order of the remaining lower- and higher-cardinality indices.
positive: Record iteration tuples for a multidimensional array with both ascending and descending declared ranges.

edge: Exit a surrounding process through an applicable disable mechanism.
notes: Include timing or explicit termination to avoid a zero-delay scheduler hang; the standard states this as a recommendation.
positive: Use a timing control in a forever body and count several repeated executions.

edge: Return an assignment-compatible expression requiring only the language's prescribed type conversion.
negative: Use bare return or an incompatible expression in a value-returning function.
positive: Return an expression matching the declared function return type.

edge: Use an X or Z Boolean filter after a successful pattern match and verify the else branch is selected.
positive: Observe the then branch for a known nonzero predicate and the else branch for zero.

edge: Place a side effect in a condition after an earlier true condition and verify it is not evaluated after chain termination.
notes: Avoid scheduling races when observing evaluation side effects.
positive: Use deterministic side effects to verify source-order condition evaluation before the first true arm.

edge: Make every condition false, with and without a trailing else, and observe the defined fallback.
positive: Make multiple chain conditions true and verify only the first true arm executes.

edge: Use a predicate combining a matches pattern and an expression with &&&.
negative: Use an if condition without parentheses or an else without a preceding if.
positive: Parse an if with multiple else-if arms, a final else, and a unique0 qualifier.

edge: Chain two matches where the second matched expression uses a binding from the first.
negative: Reference the binding in the else arm or before its declaring match clause.
positive: Bind an identifier in the first match clause and use it in a later clause and the true arm.

edge: Give a later clause a visible side effect and verify it is not evaluated after an earlier failure.
positive: Use a successful match followed by a true Boolean filter and verify the true arm.

edge: Use nested matches whose types are derived from an earlier binding.
negative: Match a structure expression against a pattern context of a different structure type.
positive: Match a tagged-union expression against a pattern of the same type.

edge: Place a separately qualified nested if inside a begin-end arm.
negative: Insert unique, unique0, or priority between else and if within an already qualified series.
positive: Qualify the initial if of a multi-arm if-else-if series.

edge: Nest a local loop inside a fork branch within an outer loop and target only the local loop.
negative: Place break or continue in a fork branch to control an enclosing loop outside the fork-join.
positive: Use break or continue within a loop wholly contained in one fork branch.

edge: Use bare return in a void subroutine and expression return in a value-returning function.
negative: Omit the terminating semicolon from a jump statement.
positive: Parse break, continue, bare return, and return with an expression in legal contexts.

edge: Omit each optional for control field and omit selected foreach index identifiers.
negative: Omit a required semicolon in a for control or the terminating semicolon of a do-while.
positive: Parse each of the six loop forms and each allowed for-step assignment form.

edge: Use an enum constant whose type matches the contextual member.
negative: Use a real-valued constant expression as a pattern leaf.
positive: Use an integral constant leaf in a pattern matched against a known integral member.

edge: Compare four-state values containing X or Z against an exactly equal constant.
positive: Match equal and unequal integral values against one constant pattern.

edge: Nest patterns and verify each binding receives its position-derived type.
negative: Use a pattern-bound identifier outside the scope established for its containing construct.
notes: Construct-specific scope extent is defined by later subclauses.
positive: Bind identifiers at differently typed structure-member positions and use them within the construct's pattern scope.

edge: Reuse the same spelling in two separate patterns with separate scopes.
negative: Reuse one binding identifier at two positions in the same pattern.
positive: Use distinct binding identifiers at two pattern positions.

edge: Cause no pattern arm to select under each qualifier and exercise the normal no-match check.
positive: Use unique-if and priority-if chains whose predicates contain matches clauses.

edge: Use a four-state constant pattern to exercise both determined success and determined failure.
positive: Match correctly typed values containing X or Z and verify every result is exactly 0 or 1.

edge: Use recursively nested patterns whose contextual types remain identical at each level.
negative: Match a structure or tagged-union value against a pattern of a different type.
positive: Match a value against a pattern with the same known contextual type.

edge: Omit every member not needed to determine the match.
negative: Make one specified nested member fail while all others match.
positive: Match a named-member structure pattern whose members are reordered and one member is omitted.

edge: Bind a four-state member value containing X and Z bits.
positive: Match a structure member with an identifier pattern and observe the full corresponding value assigned to it.

edge: Use positional and named structure patterns at different nesting levels.
negative: Supply a nested member pattern for a tagged void member.
positive: Parse nested tagged-union and named-structure patterns with identifier and wildcard leaves.

edge: Match a tagged void member, which has no nested pattern.
negative: Present a value with a different tag even if its payload bits would satisfy the nested pattern.
positive: Match the correct tagged-union member with a nested identifier or constant pattern.

edge: Use wildcards for all leaves of a nested structure pattern.
positive: Use .* at a nested member position and match values of several contents.

edge: Repeat with priority casez and priority casex where wildcard matching creates overlap.
positive: Create two matching priority-case items and verify only the source-first item's statement executes.

edge: Use condition side effects to distinguish source-order evaluation while avoiding unrelated races.
positive: Use overlapping true conditions and observe execution of the first listed priority-if arm.

edge: Place a statement in a final block and in a function to cover both containment categories.
negative: Place a procedural assignment directly at module scope rather than inside an allowed procedural block.
positive: Place an assignment statement inside each listed automatic block, a task, and a function.

edge: Exercise each statement_item alternative in a valid containing block.
negative: Use a block label followed by no statement item or terminating null semicolon.
positive: Use a labeled procedural statement and an attribute-bearing null statement in allowed procedural contexts.

edge: Control qualified-case reporting without suppressing unrelated procedural execution.
notes: Observe report presence, not diagnostic wording.
positive: Disable and re-enable qualified-case violation reporting with the applicable assertion control system task.

edge: Contrast a flushed transient overlap with a stable overlap that persists through Observed and reports.
notes: Avoid depending on active-region execution order or diagnostic wording.
positive: Create a transient qualified-case violation removed by same-time-step always_comb retriggering and verify no report.

edge: Use a compile-time-determinable no-match and accept reporting at compile time rather than requiring run-time duplication.
notes: Check report occurrence rather than wording.
positive: Run priority-case and unique-case with no matching item and verify a report.

edge: Retrigger only one caller so its pending case violation is flushed while the other caller's report matures.
positive: Execute one function containing a unique-case violation from two processes and verify independent stable reports.

edge: Retrigger one of two processes and verify only that process's pending case report is flushed.
notes: Do not depend on diagnostic wording.
positive: Create a transient qualified-case violation and retrigger its always_comb process before Observed so the pending report is discarded.

edge: Attempt a later process flush after Observed and verify it cannot cancel an already matured report.
notes: Observe report occurrence rather than wording.
positive: Maintain a qualified-case violation through Observed and verify the matured report occurs.

edge: Change relevant state later in the active region while preserving the violation to distinguish check time from report time.
notes: Use scheduler-aware observation without relying on diagnostic text.
positive: Cause a stable qualified-case violation and verify reporting is deferred until the current time step's Observed region.

edge: Control qualified-if reports without suppressing normal branch execution.
notes: Observe report presence rather than diagnostic wording.
positive: Disable and re-enable qualified-if violation reporting with the applicable assertion control system task.

edge: Contrast a transient active-region overlap with a stable overlap that must report.
notes: Materialization must avoid depending on ordering among active-region events.
positive: Create same-time active-region updates that transiently appear to violate a qualified-if check but settle without a violation.

edge: Add an explicit else and verify the no-match report is suppressed.
notes: Check report occurrence rather than wording.
positive: Drive unique-if and priority-if chains with no matching condition and no else and verify a report.

edge: Retrigger one of two callers to clear its transient failure while leaving the other caller's stable pending failure to report.
notes: Use one shared subroutine check so only calling-process identity varies.
positive: Call one function containing a unique-if violation from two processes and verify each stable failing execution reports independently.

edge: Queue multiple loop-generated violations in one process and retrigger it so the process queue is cleared together.
notes: Construct stimulus without assuming active-region execution order.
positive: Cause a transient violation in always_comb, then retrigger the process from a dependent-signal transition before Observed and verify the pending report is discarded.

edge: Retrigger the process only after report maturation and verify that this cannot flush the matured report.
notes: Oracle is report occurrence, never report wording.
positive: Leave a stable violation pending through the Observed region and verify one violation is reported.

edge: Distinguish execution-time detection from later Observed reporting with scheduler-aware state observation.
notes: Do not depend on diagnostic text.
positive: Detect a stable qualified-if violation and observe that its report matures in the same time step's Observed region.

edge: Modify data used by the captured count inside the body and verify the iteration count does not change.
positive: Repeat a body with a positive count and verify that many iterations after one count-expression evaluation.

edge: Contrast each converted-zero class with an explicit positive count.
positive: Use negative, X-containing, and Z-containing repeat counts and verify zero body executions.

edge: Use return inside a nested procedural block that is itself within a subroutine.
negative: Use return directly inside an initial, always, or module-level procedural block rather than a subroutine.
positive: Use return inside a task, void function, and value-returning function.

negative: Attempt a net declaration whose type_reference data type is not preceded by a net type keyword.
notes: Keep the declaration kind unambiguously a net when contrasting the required prefix.
positive: Declare a net with an explicit net type keyword immediately before a type_reference data type.

negative: Declare a for-loop control variable using a type_reference data type without the required var prefix.
notes: A for_variable_declaration directly exercises the chapter-12 occurrence of footnote 18.
positive: Declare a for-loop control variable with var immediately before a type_reference data type.

edge: Cause overlap while verifying the controlling expression still evaluates only once.
notes: Avoid races when observing side effects.
positive: Use deterministic counters to verify one controlling evaluation precedes item-expression evaluation.

edge: Make exactly one item match and verify no overlap report.
notes: Do not test unspecified item-expression evaluation order or diagnostic wording.
positive: Make two distinct items match and verify an overlap report.

edge: Reverse the source order of two matching items and verify the executed statement changes accordingly.
notes: Observe branch effects separately from report wording.
positive: Make two distinct items match and verify only the source-first matching statement executes.

edge: Contrast with the same expressions placed in two distinct case items, which is a violation.
positive: Put two expressions that both match in one unique-case item and verify its statement executes without an overlap violation.

edge: Make exactly one condition true and verify no overlap report.
notes: Do not rely on unspecified condition evaluation order or diagnostic wording.
positive: Make two conditions true and verify an overlap report.

edge: Reverse two true arms in source order and verify which statement executes changes accordingly.
notes: Observe arm effects independently of violation wording.
positive: Make two conditions true and verify only the source-first true arm executes.

edge: Keep overlap reporting enabled while verifying that only the no-match report is prohibited.
notes: Do not treat absence of all diagnostics as sufficient if the scenario also overlaps.
positive: Run unique0 case, casez, and casex forms with no matching item and verify no no-match report.

edge: Keep overlap checking active while isolating the no-match-only scenario.
notes: Do not depend on diagnostic wording.
positive: Drive a unique0-if chain so no condition matches and verify no no-match report.

edge: Start with zero, X, and Z conditions and verify no body execution.
positive: Start true, update the condition in the body, and verify repeated pre-test execution until false.
